text: A pipeline run is one single instance of a pipeline's execution, each with its own unique run ID. You can start one manually — also called on-demand execution — or let a trigger start it automatically instead, without you ever touching it.
Selecting New or Edit on a pipeline's Trigger menu opens the exact same configuration flow, regardless of which of the three trigger types you're actually building.

Data Factory supports three real trigger types. Schedule trigger fires on a wall-clock schedule — this lesson's topic. Tumbling window trigger fires on a periodic interval, retaining state across runs. And event-based trigger fires in response to a real event, like a file arriving in Blob Storage.

A Schedule trigger runs on a wall-clock schedule, and it's genuinely flexible about the data pattern it feeds — it doesn't distinguish time-series from non-time-series data at all. Two real pieces configure it: recurrence, the frequency and interval between runs, and an optional schedule that narrows or expands exactly when within that recurrence it actually fires.

A few patterns worth recognizing on sight: hours five means every day at five AM. Weekdays Saturday with hours seventeen means every Saturday at five PM. And month days negative one genuinely means the last day of the month, whether that's the twenty-eighth, thirtieth, or thirty-first — saving you from writing separate triggers for different month lengths.

Unlike a Tumbling window trigger, a Schedule trigger can kick off multiple pipelines, and a single pipeline can be started by multiple different triggers at once — a genuine many-to-many relationship. Next: Tumbling Window Triggers — a heavier-weight alternative, built specifically for state and reliability.
